selected.text: Is there a hell more direful than Ignorance? A hell worse than deprivation from the Divine Nearness? A hell lower than negligence and inadvertence?
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to a stranger asking whether any hell is more direful than ignorance and negligence; defines hell as deprivation.

selected.text: Negligence and apathy are heavy 'veils of Glory.'
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to Julia Grundy that negligence and apathy are heavy veils of glory; a compact image of inattention as a veil.

selected.text: Hearken unto My counsel and be not of the heedless ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief counsel to hearken to His words and be not of the heedless; a personal charge.

selected.text: yet We see ignorance and heedlessness among My loved ones
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that He sees ignorance and heedlessness among His loved ones; the clearest sign that the warning addresses believers.

selected.text: hast been awakened from the slumber of heedlessness by the breeze of His grace
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh addressing one awakened from the slumber of heedlessness by the breeze of His grace; awakening as grace.

selected.text: delivered thee from immersion in the seas of heedlessness and vain imaginings
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing one delivered from immersion in the seas of heedlessness and vain imaginings; recognition as deliverance.

selected.text: you have awakened from the sleep of negligence and have heard the heavenly melody
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá addressing one who has awakened from the sleep of negligence and heard the heavenly melody; awakening as a beginning.

selected.text: Heedlessness has seized all handmaidens except those who have transcended idle fancies
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that heedlessness has seized all handmaidens except those who transcended idle fancies; women’s recognition apart from rank.

selected.text: The clouds of idle fancies have darkened the horizon of guidance, yet these clouds are naught but the vain imaginings of heedless souls
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the clouds darkening the horizon of guidance are naught but the imaginings of heedless souls; locates the obstacle within.

selected.text: May GOD not permit any soul to become heedless. Heedlessness will uproot the foundation of man.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praying that no soul become heedless, for heedlessness uproots the foundation of man; a prayerful warning.

selected.text: And today, the essence of worldliness is heedlessness of My remembrance and love of Mine enemies
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh defining the essence of worldliness today as heedlessness of His remembrance and love of His enemies; distinguishes worldliness from particular objects.

selected.text: It has always been the practice of the heedless to hold back the sincere ones from the Cause of God
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that the heedless have always held back the sincere from the Cause of God; a necessary warning about influence.

selected.text: But if, God forbid, he becometh heedless, the treasures and riches of the earth shall profit him not
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning that if a person becomes heedless the treasures and riches of the earth shall not profit him; sets wealth against attention.

selected.text: Say: O people! The Beloved hath come and the horizons are illumined. Why do I see you among the heedless?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking the people why He sees them among the heedless now that the Beloved has come; a direct personal question.

selected.text: whenever thou findest one dejected and listless, know that he hath withered from the poisonous winds of heedlessness
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá explaining that one dejected and listless has withered from the poisonous winds of heedlessness; a distinctive application to dejection.

selected.text: yet the patients are heedless and the sick are negligent. Everyone runs after harmful remedies and each soul seeks deadly drugs.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of patients heedless of their sickness who run after harmful remedies; the guide’s healing metaphor.

selected.text: yet most are heedless thereof, for they have forsaken that which is with God and occupied themselves with that which is with them
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explaining that most are heedless because they have forsaken what is with God for what is with them; a concise cause.

selected.text: Whenever man becomes heedless of God, he is in conflict and contention with his fellow beings. Censure stems from heedlessness of Truth;
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Haifa that heedlessness of God brings conflict with others and that censure stems from it; links awareness to conduct.

selected.text: Some of the heedless ones have imagined that since the Sun of Truth has set from the horizon of the human temple, its holy rays have also declined
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejecting the imagining that the holy rays declined when the Sun of Truth set from the human temple; renewal as ongoing.

selected.text: The heedlessness of the people hath reached such a pass that after searching far and wide, they have imprisoned the Purpose of the world, and they perceive it not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that after searching far and wide the people imprisoned the Purpose of the world without perceiving it; a stark narrative irony.

selected.text: Verily your Lord, the All-Merciful, desireth to draw you nigh unto Him, yet you flee from Him. What aileth you, O heedless ones! You have slept through most of your days
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling the heedless that the All-Merciful desires to draw them near while they flee and sleep through their days; a personal call against wasted time.

selected.text: The meaning of the world of causes is the heedlessness of the servant from the One Who is served, and this has not had and does not have specification to any particular thing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh defining the world of causes as the servant’s heedlessness of the One served, not tied to any particular thing; a necessary qualification about worldliness.

selected.text: Most of those who imagine vain things have not, until now, comprehended the station of this Revelation as it deserves. This is why they wander in the wilderness of heedlessness and forgetfulness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explaining that people wander in heedlessness because they have not comprehended the station of this Revelation; gives a cause.

selected.text: By My life! Their heedlessness, remoteness, denial, and objection to Him Who created them and brought them into being sufficeth them. No punishment hath been or shall be greater than heedlessness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that no punishment has been or shall be greater than heedlessness; frames the closing reflection.

selected.text: Glory be to God! What heedlessness is this, that the fragrance from the gardens of the Kingdom of Abha hath encompassed both the seen and the unseen realms, yet the afflicted one remaineth deprived.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá exclaiming at the heedlessness of one who remains deprived though the fragrance of the Kingdom encompasses the seen and unseen; fragrance missed.

selected.text: Today the intoxication of heedlessness has seized the people of the world, and it has seized the people of the Bayan in such wise that they are seen to be more veiled than all the peoples of the earth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the people of the Bayan are seen to be more veiled than all the peoples of the earth; nearness to prophecy is no protection.

selected.text: From amongst mankind those who live a heedless life are at the end afflicted with manifest loss. For the days of their lives will come to a sudden end with no trace, no leaves, no blossom and no fruit.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a heedless life that ends suddenly with no leaves, blossom or fruit; a memorable image of a wasted life.

selected.text: Think not that those who are heedless of God are living. By My life! They are among the dead. Their wretchedness hath overcome them and their souls have prompted them to that which will lead them back to the flames.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that those heedless of God are not living but among the dead; distinguishes true life.

selected.text: Pride and turning away have become the cause and reason for negligence, for had they acted according to what the All-Merciful revealed in the Qur'an, they would have ever been observed beneath the glances of His favor.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh naming pride and turning away as the cause of negligence among those who did not act on the Qur’an; a necessary account of cause.

selected.text: But alas! man is not grateful for this supreme good, but sleeps the sleep of negligence, being careless of the great mercy which God has shown towards him, turning his face away from the light and going on his way in darkness.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: However, some of them were heedless of the influences of the Most Exalted Pen - they did not know what was the cause of this honor. Rather, they fell into heedlessness and pride and did not appreciate the value of these bounties.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Paris that some honoured through the Most Exalted Pen fell into heedlessness and pride; favour does not prevent heedlessness.

selected.text: You were as one sleeping upon the couch of heedlessness, so deep in slumber that you heard not the cry of the strivers, though that cry had encompassed all who dwell in earth and heaven, and had caused these deniers to swoon away.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling an addressee that he slept so deeply on the couch of heedlessness that he heard not the cry of the strivers; a personal reproach.

selected.text: Some of the veiled ones have imagined that the doors of heavenly bounties are closed, that the rain of great mercy hath been cut off, and that the lights of mighty grace have been extinguished. How evil is that which they imagine!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejecting the notion that the doors of heavenly bounty are closed and the rain of mercy cut off; the guide’s continuing spring.

selected.text: Alas, a hundred times alas, that the heedless are unaware of the glad tidings of this herald, and the faithless are deprived of this bounty and fruit. They have sold this brilliant crown for a mere trifle and burned this glorious diadem in the fire of negligence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of the heedless selling a brilliant crown for a trifle and burning it in the fire of negligence; a vivid picture of lost opportunity.

selected.text: But alas! we have entirely neglected them and are pursuing our own desires, following our own opinions, seeking our own ideas, and chasing our own shadows! Is it not a shame to change His Rose Garden into a bramble patch? His Delectable Paradise into a ruined abode?
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá confessing in the first person plural that we pursue our own desires and turn His Rose Garden into a bramble patch; self-examination without exemption.

selected.text: All peoples and nations are intoxicated with the wine of pride, and are heedless, oblivious and deprived of the bounties of this radiant century. Each one is wandering in some wilderness, lost in some ocean, with neither shore nor end, neither salvation nor shelter.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing peoples intoxicated with pride, each wandering in a wilderness without shore or shelter; connects pride with bewilderment.

selected.text: You had written about your shortcomings in servitude at the Sacred Threshold. This shortcoming encompasses all. 'Abdu'l-Baha also, at every moment, recites this verse in utmost shame: … "How can I raise my head in shame before the Friend, when no worthy service has been rendered by my hand
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answering a correspondent who wrote of shortcomings in servitude that this shortcoming encompasses all, himself included; carries the guide’s shared need for humility.

selected.text: But now some have shown ingratitude and become heedless of the favors of the Blessed Beauty. They attributed this progress and glory to their own good management. Therefore, in these days a great trembling has fallen upon the pillars of the Zoroastrians in Tehran. Affairs have been reversed
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá noting that some Zoroastrians of Tehran, heedless of the favours of the Blessed Beauty, attributed their progress to their own good management; a narrative of ingratitude among believers.

selected.text: beware of heedlessness … Otherwise the suckling babe is unaware of the father's bounty and the mother's care and honor and respect; nay, through ignorance and unconsciousness he may consider kindness to be harshness, honey to be poison, comfort to be pain, and the antidote to be increased suffering
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of a suckling babe who mistakes kindness for harshness and honey for poison; a memorable picture of ignorance misreading care.

selected.text: After traversing some distance in the wilderness, the fire of love became extinguished and beauty's attraction became veiled. When we passed beyond that station, we counted good deeds as evil and evil deeds as good … Each day we increased in fancy and conjecture while decreasing in attention to truth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s first-person narrative of a journey in which the fire of love was extinguished and good deeds came to be counted evil; an episode of decline from within.

selected.text: Worst of all is the people's lack of awareness, for they do not become mindful of their own deeds and character. They are drowning in the sea of heedlessness. This calamity is beyond all calamities. If they had become aware, it would have quickly passed away. But their lack of awareness causes increased confusion.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá naming the people’s unawareness of their own deeds and character as the calamity beyond all calamities; turns the inquiry toward self-examination.

selected.text: Yet despite these grievous afflictions befalling weak humanity, all remain captive to the sleep of negligence and averse to love and fellowship. There is neither awakening nor remembrance, neither thought nor contemplation, neither prayer nor supplication, neither humility and lamentation nor repentance and turning unto God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that amid grievous afflictions there is neither prayer, supplication nor repentance; connects calamity with the missing response.

selected.text: However, eyes have been veiled by the veils of tyranny, and the people of languidness have shut the eyes of justice. They cling to graves and are heedless of resurrection. They are deprived of joy and have abandoned gladness. They are in a state of negligence, distraction, sleep and slumber. They hear no voice and heed no counsel.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing people who have shut the eyes of justice, cling to graves and are heedless of resurrection; ties renewal to justice.

selected.text: When negligence overtakes a person he will become blind to everything else … In former cycles local and general negligence on the part of the people was quite prevalent but it was never so universal as now … Consider to what height the negligence of the people has soared in these days that even the mention of the name of God is tabooed
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that negligence blinds a person to everything else and has never been so universal as now; a substantive account of negligence.

selected.text: The Most Great Ocean is manifest and visible before all faces, yet they remain bereft of it and continue to thirst. The fire hath been kindled, yet they see it not. The Divine Lote Tree hath spoken, yet they hear not. The Cry hath been raised, yet they remain asleep. The horizon of the Cause hath been illumined, yet they turn not toward it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s series of images of an ocean unseen by the thirsty, a fire unseen, a Lote Tree unheard and a cry slept through; opens the sequence on a whole creation speaking.

selected.text: Alas, alas! My heedlessness hath destroyed me and my disobedience hath weakened me. I know not, O my Purpose and my Adored One, with what countenance to turn toward Thee, with what heart to approach Thy most exalted horizon and supreme height, and with what tongue to offer excuses before the manifestations of Thy justice, O Lord of all being!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s words of confession that heedlessness has destroyed and disobedience weakened the speaker before the Lord; the closing confession.

selected.text: Notwithstanding this effulgence and this diffusion of the Fragrance of Rose-Garden of the Covenant, innumerable souls are yet afflicted with the sleep of negligence. The eyes are veiled and the nostrils do not inhale the fragrant perfume. What a negligence is this! What an inadvertence is this! What an ignorance is this and what a heedlessness is this!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that souls sleep despite the fragrance of the Rose-Garden of the Covenant; a memorable exclamation on negligence.

selected.text: They that are sunk in heedlessness fondly imagine that massacre and crucifixion cause the fire of the Word of God to be extinguished, and regard martyrdom as a devastating injury. They are utterly oblivious of the truth that through such afflictions the Cause of God is exalted, its fame is blazoned far and wide, and the martyrs themselves are enabled to attain the boundless retreats of nearness unto God.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Now must the sincere ones and the pure in heart, with utmost lowliness, beseech God, exalted be His glory, for the protection of the radiant Faith. The recompense of deeds is evident and manifest at all times, but where is the soul who will take heed, and where is the one who will be awakened? The sleep of heedlessness and the intoxication of pride have seized all and cast them like uprooted stones upon the earth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling the sincere to beseech God with lowliness for the protection of the Faith and asking where is the one who will be awakened; joins prayer and warning.

selected.text: Days have passed and We have not heard from the bird of thy heart the melodies of love, nor have We found from thee the sweet savors of longing and affection. It is as though thou hast forgotten Us and forgotten the stations of reunion while the breezes of grace wafted upon thee. And if thou forgettest Us, verily We do not forget thee, and if thou art heedless of Our remembrance, verily We are not heedless of thee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s assurance that if the addressee forgets Him, He does not forget him; the guide’s closing assurance of remembrance.

selected.text: A hundred thousand regrets that most of the people are heedless of what they see and hear. The Most Great Bell hath been adorned by the fingers of the mercy of the All-Merciful in the midmost heart and the divine call hath been raised. Yet the people are seen to be withered, nay rather dead, save whom thy Lord willeth. Do they not inhale the fragrance of the utterance and remain heedless, or are they deprived by what their hands have wrought?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Most Great Bell sounded by the fingers of mercy while the people are withered; a memorable image of the call.

selected.text: Ages have passed and your precious lives are well-nigh ended, yet not a single breath of purity hath reached Our court of holiness from you. Though immersed in the ocean of misbelief, yet with your lips ye profess the one true faith of God. Him whom I abhor ye have loved, and of My foe ye have made a friend. Notwithstanding, ye walk on My earth complacent and self-satisfied, heedless that My earth is weary of you and everything within it shunneth you.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Yet some commanding souls, unwittingly following their own desires, are engaged in undermining the Cause of God, counting themselves among the mature and perfect ones. The cawing of the crows, which was revealed in numerous Tablets and about which We gave warning, is in these days raised from certain quarters. Although these are days wherein fellowship, unity, love and accord are beloved, those heedless souls have again become the cause of differences.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning that some commanding souls, counting themselves mature, undermine the Cause and again become a cause of differences; the warning addressed to believers.

selected.text: This fairest of lands was once a lamp, streaming with the rays of Divine knowledge, of science and art, of nobility and high achievement, of wisdom and valor. Today, because of the idleness and lethargy of her people, their torpor, their undisciplined way of life, their lack of pride, lack of ambition -- her bright fortune has been totally eclipsed, her light has turned to darkness. "The seven heavens and the seven earths weep over the mighty when he is brought low
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Some are awakened and become aware of divine intentions, their awareness increasing, while others grow more heedless. In these days, were one to find hearing, every created thing would inform man of the mighty events and grievous trials which are the consequences of deeds, and would, in most eloquent language, make him aware. How many a stone hath melted from the fear of God, and how many a servant laugheth and playeth until chastisement seizeth him from every direction.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that some awaken while others grow more heedless, and that every created thing would warn a hearing person of the consequences of deeds; links attention to consequence.

selected.text: when men of renown were immersed in manifest idle fancies
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: the ears of the world are occupied with listening to unworthy tales
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s observation that the ears of the world are occupied with unworthy tales; a brief image of distracted hearing.

selected.text: How long will ye follow vain imaginings and idle fancies? Open your eyes!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s brief call to stop following vain imaginings and open one’s eyes; the guide’s plainest summons to independent sight.

selected.text: The abundance of bounty and blessing hath become the cause of heedlessness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the abundance of bounty and blessing has become the cause of heedlessness; the guide’s opening paradox.

selected.text: The heedless people pass their days in hopes whose fulfillment is impossible.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that the heedless pass their days in hopes whose fulfillment is impossible; a concise image of vain hope.

selected.text: The way of God and the religion of God have ceased to be of any worth in the eyes of men.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Be not grieved by the opposition of people and their turning away, for they are weak and immature.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling not to be grieved at people’s opposition, for they are weak and immature; patience toward others.

selected.text: Grieve not over the condition of those who are heedless today. Soon shall they bewail their own souls.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling an addressee not to grieve over the heedless, who shall soon bewail their own souls; counsel against despair.

selected.text: of the Manifestation of the Lord of Hosts. All the people of the world are buried in the graves of nature, or are slumbering, heedless and unaware
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The world is heedless - be ye aware. All are asleep - be ye wakeful. All are stupefied - be ye conscious.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s charge that the world is heedless, so be ye aware, and all are asleep, so be ye wakeful; turns diagnosis into vocation.

selected.text: Yet those who were invited did not respond to the call, due to their ignorance, heedlessness, pride and vainglory.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that those invited did not respond because of ignorance, heedlessness, pride and vainglory; names the causes of refusal.

selected.text: This is the Day wherein the birds warble, seized by the rapture of the Manifestation, yet the people perceive not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of birds warbling in rapture at the Manifestation while the people perceive not; adds birdsong to creation’s voice.

selected.text: The fragrances of divine revelation have permeated the world, yet the servants remain heedless and veiled therefrom.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the fragrances of revelation permeating the world while the servants remain veiled; adds fragrance to the sensory imagery.

selected.text: these days wherein God calleth aloud with the most exalted call: "Unto Me, unto Me, O concourse of the heedless ones!"
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recording God’s call, “Unto Me, unto Me, O concourse of the heedless ones!”; the divine call addressed to the heedless themselves.

selected.text: yet the people remain in heedlessness and hypocrisy. Among them is he who sees a straw as silver and darkness as light
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s picture of one who sees a straw as silver and darkness as light; a memorable image of distorted perception.

selected.text: They imagine they see, but I swear by My life they are a blind people. They hear the call of God, yet turn away from it.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that those who imagine they see are a blind people; states the guide’s problem of confident unawareness.

selected.text: Associate with the people, for they know not - had they known, they would circle round the Cause at eventide and at dawn.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding the friends associate with the people, for they know not; the guide’s counsel of fellowship with the unaware.

selected.text: How many an ignorant one claimeth knowledge without proof or clear Book, and how many a transgressor claimeth faith in God!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting how many ignorant ones claim knowledge without proof and how many transgressors claim faith in God; pairs false learning with false devotion.

selected.text: In the farthest regions of America souls have awakened while the people of Iran are still caught in the sleep of negligence.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá noting that souls in the farthest regions of America have awakened while the people of Iran sleep; distance from the source is no barrier.

selected.text: Most of the people of the earth today are heedless and veiled, while thou, through God's grace, art assured and turning toward Him.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh assuring an addressee that while most are heedless and veiled he, through God’s grace, is turning toward Him; awakening as a gift.

selected.text: Glory be to God! Such heedlessness hath seized the people of Iran that they have taken abasement for glory and loss for mighty gain.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that heedlessness has led people to take abasement for glory and loss for mighty gain; inverted values.

selected.text: How many among the great ones and the learned are today heedless of the Self-Subsisting and deprived of the Choice Wine that is sealed.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting how many great and learned ones are heedless of the Self-Subsisting today; formal learning no guarantee.

selected.text: But alas, the people of that land are still heedless and unaware. Soon they will awaken, become conscious, and express pride and glory.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá saying the people of that land are still heedless but will soon awaken and take pride in it; hope for awakening.

selected.text: The Beloved of the world of being is present in this land, but they are oblivious. All are heedless; all are unaware; all are uninformed.
selected.reason: Words of Bahá’u’lláh recollected by Mirza Habibu’llah Afnan that the Beloved is present in this land and all are unaware; a reported voice kept distinct.

selected.text: But alas, a thousand times alas! The eyes see it not, the ears are deaf, and the hearts and minds are oblivious of this supreme bestowal.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Some negligent men think that the spring season has concluded and nothing but winter remains. They are immersed in their own vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Abu Sinan that some negligent men think the spring has ended and only winter remains; anticipates the continuing spring.

selected.text: Would that the servants knew! Would that the people understood! For if they became aware and discovered the Purpose, all would turn toward Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s wish that the servants knew, for if they discovered the Purpose all would turn toward Him; sets hope beside the diagnosis.

selected.text: The eyes of the world have been afflicted with the ophthalmia of vain imaginings, depriving them from beholding the lights of the Sun of Truth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the world’s eyes afflicted with the ophthalmia of vain imaginings; a memorable image.

selected.text: The world was created for the recognition of the Ancient King, yet its people denied the divine proof and rose up in ingratitude for His favors.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the world was created for the recognition of the Ancient King, yet its people rose up in ingratitude; gratitude as responsibility.

selected.text: Such a heavenly Gift God brought for them, but they did not appreciate it. Such Divine Music was played for them, but they did not listen to it.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Tiberias that people did not appreciate a heavenly gift or listen to the divine music played for them; the guide’s image of unheard music.

selected.text: We see them in heedlessness and in their ancient stupor. Do thou remind them with wisdom, that perchance My wondrous remembrance may influence them.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding an addressee remind the heedless with wisdom, that His remembrance may influence them; practical counsel.

selected.text: Behold! The things that had been mentioned in the Books of old have now appeared, and yet the people, though they look upon them, comprehend them not!
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: All heard the call, but with contaminated ears; for had they hearkened with attentive ears, they would surely have been enabled to turn and draw near.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that all heard the call but with contaminated ears, whereas attentive hearing would have drawn them near; distinguishes hearing from hearkening.

selected.text: The world is in motion through the magnetic force of the Word of the Lord of Eternity, yet the servants remain heedless thereof, save whom God willeth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the world set in motion by the magnetic force of the Word while the servants remain heedless; a distinctive image of unnoticed attraction.

selected.text: This is naught but due to the heedlessness of souls, else the sun is far distinct from the shadow, and the flower is clearly evident from its likeness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that only heedlessness keeps souls from distinguishing the sun from the shadow and the flower from its likeness; discernment.

selected.text: This is the Day of Resurrection, yet the people perceive it not. This is the Day of Loss and Gain, and of Recompense, yet most among mankind know it not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring this the Day of Resurrection, of loss and gain and recompense, while the people perceive it not; names the Day the people awaited.

selected.text: They appear as sheep that have lost their shepherd, scattered and distracted, wandering in the wilderness of heedlessness and ignorance, and are unaware.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh likening people to sheep that have lost their shepherd, scattered in the wilderness of heedlessness; a memorable pastoral image.

selected.text: Notwithstanding this, the people are negligent and indifferent, eyes are blinded, ears are deaf, nostrils are choked and understandings are unawakened
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing eyes blinded, ears deaf and understandings unawakened; gathers the guide’s sensory imagery in one sentence.

selected.text: All awaited the days of attainment, yet when the Self-Sufficient, the Most High, appeared, they turned away from Him and followed every ignorant remote one
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that all awaited the days of attainment yet turned away when He appeared; opens the gap between expectation and recognition.

selected.text: The ignorance of God's creatures hath darkened the resplendent horizon of knowledge; the heedlessness of the people hath veiled the radiant dawn of guidance.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s paired statement that ignorance has darkened the horizon of knowledge and heedlessness has veiled the dawn of guidance; a concise formulation.

selected.text: Despite this, half a century has elapsed while humanity remains in continuous slumber. What heedlessness is this! What ignorance! What loss! What deprivation!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá exclaiming that after half a century humanity remains in continuous slumber; marks the duration of unawareness.

selected.text: At the time of each Manifestation of God the people were heedless and ignorant of the truth except for a few who investigated and understood the divine words.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to a Jewish lady that at each Manifestation only a few who investigated understood the divine words; connects recognition with personal investigation.

selected.text: Think not ill of God, and be not of those who through false learned ones remain heedless of God's religion and turn not unto the religion of God, the Most High.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh counselling not to be among those who through false learned ones remain heedless of God’s religion; a warning against borrowed authority.

selected.text: Reflect upon the heedlessness of the people, who all utter the words "May God hasten His coming," yet not a single soul hath understood what this allusion signifieth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that all say May God hasten His coming, yet none understands what it signifies; words repeated without understanding.

selected.text: The heedless people are themselves the preventers of divine bounties, and through their impure deeds and false words have deprived themselves of God's infinite favors.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the heedless are themselves the preventers of divine bounties through impure deeds and false words; locates responsibility in conduct.

selected.text: Mankind are naturally heedless and prone to commit injustice and excess. They do not turn their faces toward God and do not let their hearts be swayed by ideal emotions.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Abu Sinan that mankind are naturally heedless and prone to injustice and excess; links unawareness with conduct.

selected.text: When the law of prayer was revealed in the time of the Messenger, the idolaters would prevent their ears from hearing the call to prayer and would count hearing it as evil.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalling idolaters who stopped their ears against the call to prayer in the time of the Messenger; a historical example of refusing to hear.

selected.text: the heedlessness of the peoples of the world hath reached such a pass that they distinguish not between good and evil, nor do they differentiate between truth and falsehood
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that heedlessness has reached such a pass that people distinguish neither good from evil nor truth from falsehood; the cost to moral discernment.

selected.text: The whole world speaketh His Name yet is veiled from Him, turneth toward His countenance yet is debarred from Him, maketh mention of His Name yet is heedless of His Command.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s statement that the whole world speaks His Name yet is veiled from Him and heedless of His Command; the section’s theme in one sentence.

selected.text: The gift of God consists in all glory and wisdom, vision and hearing. But what benefit is there when the foolish pursue blindness and deafness and muteness and estrangement?
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting God’s gift of vision and hearing with the foolish pursuit of blindness, deafness and muteness; frames heedlessness as a gift refused.

selected.text: Until now, God's purpose remaineth unknown to the people of the cities of tyranny and oppression. They wander in the wilderness of heedlessness and traverse the valley of greed
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that God’s purpose remains unknown in the cities of tyranny, whose people wander in heedlessness and greed; links heedlessness with injustice.

selected.text: The deed is manifest and His grace evident, and yet the people persist in obvious falsehood. Well is it with him who hath heard and responded, and woe betide the heedless ones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh blessing the one who has heard and responded and warning the heedless; the section’s call to response.

selected.text: It is amazing that people are afraid of physical plagues, but have no worries of spiritual calamities. They are heedless of being inflicted with a myriad of spiritual catastrophes
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Abu Sinan that people fear physical plagues but not spiritual calamities; a distinctive comparison.

selected.text: How many kings and subjects, sovereigns and queens awaited the Days of God, yet after the appearance of the Divine Day all were occupied with their own desires and veiled from Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting how many kings, queens and subjects awaited the Days of God yet were occupied with their own desires; shows that rank gives no protection.

selected.text: What regret and remorse that people should deprive themselves of the outpourings of the Divine Day! … Say: Ponder on that which hath been sent down for you and be not of the heedless
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that people deprive themselves of the Divine Day and bidding them ponder what has been sent down; a call to reflect.

selected.text: of the Goal of all worlds have been and are beloved. The lovers in all regions know the value of this station. Night and day We have summoned the servants to that which would cause the elevation of the Word and the advancement of souls. Yet most were found heedless, nay, turned away
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounting that He summoned the servants night and day to what would elevate the Word and advance souls; the responsibility the call carries.

selected.text: Glory be to God! The proofs of the world bow down in prostration while the servants remain heedless. All things are engaged in glorification and praise, yet the people remain deprived.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that all things glorify and praise God while the servants remain deprived; contrasts creation’s praise with human absence.

selected.text: Men of might and valor remain unaware of the cause of their own creation, for had they become conscious of it, they would not have deprived themselves of the dawning of the divine light
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that men of might and valor remain unaware of the cause of their own creation; prestige does not confer insight.

selected.text: The peoples of the world, despite their searching and expectation, are observed to be heedless. The people are occupied with the people, and remain heedless of and veiled from the Truth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the people are occupied with the people and veiled from the Truth despite their searching; a distinctive diagnosis of social distraction.

selected.text: They hear the Call of God, then deny it. Verily, they know not. They behold the Most Great Relief, yet they understand not. They follow their vain desires and imagine they are doing good.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing people who hear the Call, deny it, follow their desires and imagine they are doing good; self-deception in conduct.

selected.text: and with every passing moment, this musk-laden breeze will shed its perfume upon the world. But alas! The people of Persia remain wrapt in heedless slumber and, like the blind and the deaf, neither see the Light nor hear the Call. They are
