selected.text: We have sent down the verses and manifested the signs, but most of the people know not. We beseech God to assist those who are heedless today and draw them nigh unto this forbidden station.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh beseeching God to assist those heedless today and draw them near; a prayer for others.

selected.text: and made known to us remedies that purify and tranquillize and soothe. And all this, so that the feeble frame of the world might be freed from the burning thirst of error and ignorance, and this afflicted body might be delivered from the sore distress of heedlessness and impotence
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: The world has been honored by the call of My Name, the Self-Subsisting, yet the people remain behind a thick veil. How many learned ones have turned away from God, how many heroes have opposed Him
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting how many learned ones have turned away from God and how many heroes have opposed Him; learning and valour no protection.

selected.text: Although the people are observed to be in such heedlessness that its mention is beyond both pen and tongue, yet the divine Will and Purpose has been and shall ever be triumphant and all-pervading.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh affirming that despite heedlessness beyond description the divine Will remains triumphant and all-pervading; hope amid warning.

selected.text: But alas, the sleeping did not awaken, the deaf did not hear, the blind did not see, the frozen did not ignite, and the ignorant did not learn. This is everlasting regret and this is endless loss.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá lamenting that the sleeping did not awaken, the deaf did not hear and the ignorant did not learn; warning summed up as everlasting regret.

selected.text: Behold the people and their heedlessness - they have taken the drop and cast the ocean behind them. Thus have their souls enticed them, and they are today among the transgressors in My mighty Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people have taken the drop and cast the ocean behind them; a memorable image of misplaced choice.

selected.text: O concourse of creation! The Greatest Veil hath been rent asunder and the Greatest Scene hath been adorned through the revelation of God, the Lord of Destiny; yet most of the people remain heedless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh announcing that the Greatest Veil has been rent asunder yet most people remain heedless; marks the gap between disclosure and response.

selected.text: This was a general rule in all dispensations and cycles that strangers would become familiar while those familiar ones who were from the homeland of the Manifestation of Truth would remain strangers.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating the general rule that strangers become familiar while those of the Manifestation’s homeland remain strangers; a necessary qualification about familiarity.

selected.text: Observe mankind and their lack of recognition - they deny him who enjoineth upon them what is right, and condemn him who desireth their preservation in the kingdom of God, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people deny the one who enjoins what is right and condemn the one who desires their preservation; responsibility toward counsel.

selected.text: The fragrance of the garment has wafted through creation, yet the people remain in far-off heedlessness. The breezes of spring have blown in the days of God, yet the people remain behind a thick veil.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s image of the fragrance of the garment and the breezes of spring while people remain behind a thick veil; prepares the guide’s springtime theme.

selected.text: And when We manifested the Cause, the hearts of the mighty were seized with trembling, and the foundations of princes were shaken. Yet the people remain dead, shrouded in the veils of their own selves.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounting that the hearts of the mighty trembled when the Cause was manifested, yet the people remain dead in the veils of self; political events and spiritual response.

selected.text: Consider how they prostrate themselves on the sands that at one time may have been honored by the footsteps of Christ and His Apostles, but are now heedless of the Lord of Hosts! Amazing, amazing, amazing!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Abu Sinan on people prostrating on sands once honoured by Christ’s footsteps while heedless of the Lord of Hosts; a narrative example of misplaced reverence.

selected.text: Most people cling to their own vain imaginings and remain heedless of the Sovereign of verses. They have preferred conjecture to true knowledge and have contented themselves with doubt instead of certitude
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that most people have preferred conjecture to true knowledge and doubt to certitude; a clear statement of supposition mistaken for knowledge.

selected.text: These are days wherein all have taken their vain desires as their god and dust as the Lord of Lords. In such circumstances, whom should the Pen mention and by what merit should the Tongue of Grandeur sing?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that all have taken their vain desires as their god and dust as the Lord of Lords; names desire as an idol.

selected.text: In this time the affliction of cholera has encompassed all regions of Iran, that perchance the heedless might become aware. But what use, for the reproofs of the All-Loving Lord have no effect on hard rock
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá noting that cholera spread through Iran that the heedless might become aware, yet reproofs have no effect on hard rock; calamity as unheeded reminder.

selected.text: Notwithstanding all this I do see very few who are really mindful; nay rather day by day their negligence is increased. Few are praying or supplicating or invoking God to turn away these ordeals from mankind
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá that few are praying for these ordeals to be turned away from mankind; calls for prayer for others amid trial.

selected.text: Pay no attention to the fact that the people of London are caught in heedlessness - indeed all the world is afflicted with self-interest and selfish desires and is occupied day and night with worldly pursuits
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá counselling a correspondent to pay no attention to London’s heedlessness, since all the world is afflicted with self-interest; guards against contempt for one place.

selected.text: The very rocks have testified to the Lord of all being, yet the people remain behind a mighty veil. There is nothing that hath not borne witness to this Cause, yet the people persist in manifest doubt
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the very rocks have testified to the Lord of all being while the people remain veiled; carries the image of creation bearing witness.

selected.text: Were the people to know, they would expend all they possess, even their very souls, that My Most Exalted Pen might move upon their names, yet today they remain veiled by following the daysprings of idle fancies
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that if people knew they would spend all they possess that His Pen might move upon their names; the worth of being remembered.

selected.text: He who is heedless knoweth not the sweetness of wakefulness … They run from the wise to the heedless, and from the learned to the ignorant. They distinguish not between what harmeth them and what profiteth them
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that the heedless know not the sweetness of wakefulness and run from the wise to the ignorant; shows the inability to tell harm from benefit.

selected.text: Yet when it shone forth from the horizon of the world, most of mankind turned away, save those souls who broke the chains of imitation through the name of the Almighty and turned toward the horizon of the Cause.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing souls who broke the chains of imitation and turned toward the Cause; links recognition with freedom from blind imitation.

selected.text: Every stone and clod of earth hath spoken that which the Book hath spoken, yet the people remain in doubt and dissension. When the Call was raised, they turned away and clung to their own idle fancies and vain imaginings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that every stone and clod has spoken what the Book has spoken, yet people cling to their own fancies; creation and scripture speak together.

selected.text: Indeed, the face of the world hath been turned toward irreligion. In all years, nay in all months, nay in all days, it hath been far from faith, certitude and knowledge, and close to conjecture and vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that the face of the world has turned toward irreligion, far from certitude and close to conjecture; a broad diagnosis.

selected.text: Today the people are seen to be blind and deaf, save the soul who, through the breezes of the grace of the Dawn of Manifestation, lifted its head from the couch of heedlessness and turned toward the supreme horizon.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing people as blind and deaf save the soul that lifts its head from the couch of heedlessness; leaves room for awakening.

selected.text: This is the Day wherein the Mother Book speaks, yet most of the people neither know nor hear. The proof has been perfected and the Cry has been raised and the Rock has cried out, yet most of the people are heedless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that the Mother Book speaks and the Rock cries out while most neither know nor hear; gathers proof and cry together.

selected.text: The eye of creation hath not witnessed any more heedless than these, for they deny that whereby they pride themselves above all the peoples of the earth and whereby their faith is established, yet they perceive not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that people deny the very thing on which they pride themselves and on which their faith is established; the paradox of devotion.

selected.text: Nevertheless, most people remain veiled and heedless. The cause of this heedlessness are those souls who, in former ages and countless centuries, prevented people from the Kawthar of the utterance of the All-Merciful.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh tracing present heedlessness to souls who in former ages kept people from the utterance of the All-Merciful; carries the relation between leaders and followers.

selected.text: The cause and reason for the veiling of the people hath been and will continue to be the most great veil, which is the ignorance that the ignorant ones of the earth have bound unto themselves in the name of knowledge.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh identifying the most great veil as the ignorance bound on in the name of knowledge; introduces the guide’s theme of misplaced certainty.

selected.text: By the life of God! The eyes and ears were created to behold and hearken in this Day, but the heedless and ignorant servants have become veiled. They have prevented the letter from the word, and the word from the Book.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh declaring that eyes and ears were created to behold and hearken in this Day; restates the purpose of the faculties.

selected.text: Today the ocean of bounty is surging and the sun of grace is shining, yet people remain prevented. For ages and centuries they awaited His appearance, yet when He was made manifest they arose to shed His most pure blood
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalling that those who awaited His appearance for centuries arose to shed His blood; the gravest form of the paradox.

selected.text: We have sent down the verses and manifested the clear proofs, yet most of the people hear not. They have cast away that for which they were created and have taken up that which was forbidden unto them in the Book of God
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people have cast away that for which they were created and taken up what was forbidden; links heedlessness to human purpose.

selected.text: the Divine Lote-Tree calleth out with the loudest voice, yet most of the people remain heedless. They who are heedless this day of My choice sealed wine - these have no portion in God's Book, the Mighty, the All-Praised
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh warning that those heedless this day of His choice sealed wine have no portion in God’s Book; states the stakes of the call.

selected.text: Glory be to God! What heedlessness hath encompassed the hearts and minds! After witnessing and observing the world of power, might, mercy and bounty, they pass it by and occupy themselves with matters unworthy of mention.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that people pass by the world of power, mercy and bounty to occupy themselves with matters unworthy of mention; opens the section on distraction.

selected.text: As for those who have forbidden themselves the spiritual feast and the breaths of the Spirit of God, they are dead, not living, and for them there is no permanence, neither in this worldly abode nor in the Kingdom of God.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that those who forbid themselves the spiritual feast are dead, with no permanence in this world or the Kingdom; spiritual life and death distinguished.

selected.text: O Haydar! Upon thee be the glory of God, and the glory of the heaven of My mercy, and the sun of My favors. The heedlessness of the people hath reached such a pass that the Kingdom of Utterance hath been bidden to silence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling Haydar that the heedlessness of the people has caused the Kingdom of Utterance to be bidden to silence; a striking consequence.

selected.text: Yet some have been hindered by their selfish desires, such that thou dost witness that although, by the belief of all, mankind was created specifically for the knowledge of God, they remain veiled from Him and turn to others.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that, though all believe mankind was created for the knowledge of God, selfish desires keep them veiled; links desire to purpose.

selected.text: yet the people deny and perceive not. The fragrance of the Beloved hath wafted throughout the world, yet the people detect it not. The mysteries have been revealed and the signs have appeared, yet the servants understand not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the fragrance of the Beloved has wafted throughout the world yet people detect it not; joins fragrance with mysteries revealed.

selected.text: But in this mighty century when the call was raised from the Blessed Tree of Anisa, the Divine Lote Tree, the Beauty of Abha, most turned away and brought forth a hundred thousand excuses and objections and closed their eyes.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observing that when the call was raised most turned away with a hundred thousand excuses and closed their eyes; names the excuses that hinder recognition.

selected.text: Yet the people hear not. The veils have covered their sight, and the clouds have enshrouded their eyes. Lo! They understand not. They behold the Lord of Lords established upon the throne of might, yet from Him they turn aside.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing veils over sight and clouds over eyes, so that people behold the Lord of Lords yet turn aside; a full picture of seeing without perceiving.

selected.text: The world is receptive and its people are heedless. They seek after thorns and thistles - that is, vain imaginings and idle fancies - while turning away from the pearls of utterance, clinging instead to pebbles and date-stones.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing a receptive world whose people seek thorns, thistles and pebbles while turning from the pearls of utterance; a memorable image.

selected.text: At present the representatives are heedless and know not from whence this melody comes, nor that this light emanates from the Sun of Reality. But eventually they will know, eventually they will acknowledge and confess this truth
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá stating that the representatives are now heedless but will eventually know and acknowledge the truth; sets hope beside criticism.

selected.text: God has made such a glorious Sun as this to shine from the horizon of the East, and yet the Persians are still fast asleep. How often has perpetual fortune knocked at a person's door, only for him to reject it with all his might!
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Vienna that perpetual fortune knocks at a person’s door only to be rejected; a memorable image of a missed opportunity.

selected.text: the advent of the Messiah. It has been two thousand years since the Messiah appeared, and yet the Jews continue to wait. Observe what unawareness does! They set their expectations on the text of Isaiah---that the Messiah would come from the skies, an unknown place, and that, when He came, He would break the mountains apart and cause a mighty earthquake
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in London on the Jews still awaiting a Messiah expected, from the text of Isaiah, to come from the skies; shows literal expectation hindering recognition.

selected.text: Despite the healing counsels and conclusive admonitions that have been sent down from the Source of Divine Unity in the revealed scriptures, they are seen to be more remote than previous nations and more heedless than all who dwell on earth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that despite healing counsels and conclusive admonitions some are more remote and heedless than previous nations; counsel received does not guarantee response.

selected.text: Today the opposers of this Cause show the same heedlessness. While the Cause is spreading with the swiftness of lightning, and its great light is blessing nations, its enemies attempt to resist its strength and prevent its beneficent effects.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá to pilgrims that opposers show the same heedlessness while the Cause spreads like lightning; connects past and present opposition.

selected.text: In Persia we see now the beginning of heedlessness and the first manifestations of neglecting religion. If this state of things is not stopped by the power of the divine teachings, it will soon be chaos and distress, eternal vileness and shame.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá warning that the neglect of religion beginning in Persia will lead to chaos and distress unless stopped by the divine teachings; the social consequence of heedlessness.

selected.text: yet the heedless people remain veiled from the Truth and occupied with vain imaginings, appearing like the peoples of former times. We beseech God to grant justice that they may not be deprived of the outpourings of the True Bestower in His days.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh beseeching God to grant justice to the heedless that they may not be deprived of His outpourings; a prayer for others.

selected.text: The Book of God speaketh the truth, yet the people remain heedless. The eye of creation hath never beheld the like of their condition. The wine of idle fancy hath so seized them that they have been prevented from recognizing the Lord of all beings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the wine of idle fancy has kept people from recognizing the Lord of all beings; the image of intoxication as heedlessness.

selected.text: How veiled are the people! … Every hour during the days of Christ they raised a thousand doubts; by every means they sought to undermine the Cause of Christ. Now throughout all regions they give glad tidings in His name. Such is the state of mankind
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá contrasting the doubts raised against Christ in His days with the glad tidings now given in His name; shows recognition shifting over time.

selected.text: And the Lord of Sinai speaketh and most of the people know not. They pass by the signs and look not. They behold the Most Great Scene and yet turn away from it. They come before the Countenance and recognize not. They hear the Call and perceive not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing people who pass by the signs, come before the Countenance and recognize not; a litany of missed encounter.

selected.text: All the people are asleep. Why are they so negligent and neglectful of the glorious destiny which His Holiness Baha'u'llah has appointed for them? They must turn their faces toward the Kingdom of Abha; instead they are asleep upon the bed of negligence.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá at the Baltimore Hotel asking why people neglect the glorious destiny Bahá’u’lláh appointed for them; a call to turn toward the Kingdom.

selected.text: the perfect man: that his nature and his character be sugar and honey. Grace beseemeth him, not wrath; sweetness becometh him, not venom. But what can be done? Souls are heedless and ignorant. Therefore do they crave the savage, seek the shedder of blood and the bloodthirsty, and desire the tyrant and the treacherous. What ignorance is this, what folly and heedlessness in the world
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the perfect man, whose nature is sugar and honey and who shows grace rather than wrath, while heedless souls crave the tyrant; kindness as the response.

selected.text: They will awaken when the caravan has reached its destination, taken shelter in the precinct of the Beloved, and found repose beneath the pavilion of sanctity - while those ignorant and unaware ones remain lost and wandering at the first step of the path
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of the heedless awakening only when the caravan has reached its destination; the urgency of timely response.

selected.text: Such is the state and station of those souls who have followed their own selves and desires, and remained heedless of the ultimate goal and the most exalted horizon. Fie upon them for what their hands have wrought in the days of God, the Lord of the worlds!
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the state of those who followed their own selves and desires and were heedless of the ultimate goal; closes the section on its moral cause.

selected.text: Today the clouds of vain desires of heedless souls have become an obstacle and prevented people from the Horizon of Divine Unity. Had they but known, they would have cast away all they possess and hastened with their hearts unto God, the Lord of the worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that the clouds of vain desires have prevented people from the Horizon of Divine Unity; desire as obstruction.

selected.text: yet most of the people understand not. We have adorned the world with the ornament of My Most Great Name, yet the nations hasten in the wilderness of heedlessness. They behold the proof of God yet deny it, and witness His clear tokens yet turn away from them.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing nations hastening in the wilderness of heedlessness, beholding the proof of God yet denying it; closes the sequence on seeing and denying.

selected.text: The horizon of the world hath been illumined by the Sun of My Most Great Name, yet most of the people perceive not. The verses have filled all regions, yet the people recognize not. The atoms have testified to the Revealer of verses, yet the people hear not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that verses fill all regions and atoms testify to the Revealer while the people hear not; restates creation’s witness.

selected.text: Glory be to God! Where has vision gone and with what thoughts is the heart occupied, that at every moment the veils of heedlessness are seen to grow thicker? They have strayed from God's straight path and clung to the ways of idle fancies and vain imaginings.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking where vision has gone that the veils of heedlessness grow thicker at every moment; heedlessness as a deepening habit.

selected.text: Yet the people remain heedless and veiled, and until now have not reflected upon what has been and is the cause of these events and tribulations. Their eyes have been blinded and their tongues have been silenced, and today they neither understand nor perceive.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people have not reflected on the cause of these events and tribulations; links calamity to reflection.

selected.text: Although at every moment the world informeth man through its changes of its own extinction and maketh him aware of its passing, yet all are heedless and veiled. They were not stirred by the breezes of the spring of revelation, as if they were uprooted palm-trunks.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that the world announces its own passing at every moment yet people remain unstirred, like uprooted palm-trunks; mortality ignored.

selected.text: Be thou steadfast in the remembrance of thy Lord and speaking forth His Name amongst His slumbering servants who, when the Call was raised, were seized by the intoxication of vain desires in such wise that they became heedless of that for which they were created.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh bidding an addressee be steadfast in remembrance and speak His Name among the slumbering servants; an enacted response.

selected.text: Strange it is that while the Dawn hath appeared and a sweet-scented breeze wafteth with utmost delicacy and gentleness from the direction of the Robe, yet the people of the earth remain heedless and veiled therefrom. A dark smoke hath prevented most from beholding.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that the Dawn has appeared and a sweet breeze wafts while a dark smoke prevents most from beholding; fragrance and obscuring smoke.

selected.text: How many a queen besought her Lord and desired from Him the encounter with His Manifestation in His days, yet when He appeared she was found among the heedless. Thus did the days pass and the matter was accomplished, but most of the people remain among the heedless.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that a queen who besought the encounter with His Manifestation was found among the heedless when He appeared; rank gives no protection.

selected.text: are heedless and know not the fruits, mysteries and traces of the mention of God, exalted be His glory. For were the fruits of but one letter thereof to be cast upon those on earth, by God Himself the Truth, all would turn, detached from all else, to the most exalted horizon. O friend! The intoxication of heedlessness has seized all and deprived them of the outpourings of the All-Bountiful, save whom thy Lord willeth
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh telling a friend that the fruits of a single letter of God’s remembrance would turn all to the most exalted horizon; the power of remembrance.

selected.text: Despite this, for these blameworthy people the means of awakening become the cause of increased heedlessness. They are like children for whom the rocking of the cradle causes deeper sleep - that is, the movement which should cause awakening results in increased slumber.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s image of children whom the rocking of the cradle sends into deeper sleep; explains how the means of awakening can increase heedlessness.

selected.text: The heedlessness of the servants hath prevented the divine bounty, and although the errors of the world cannot withhold the Ancient Lord from bestowing His grace, yet the people have deprived their own selves of the wondrous tokens of His mercy, favor and loving-kindness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh explaining that the errors of the world cannot withhold divine grace, yet people deprive their own selves of it; responsibility for one’s own deprivation.

selected.text: Yet the foolish among the witless say that the Day of the Lord hath passed and darkness hath encompassed all and the pitch-black night hath descended and the lights of the Most Glorious Beauty have set. This is but error and blindness. They have eyes but see not with them
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá rejecting the claim that the Day of the Lord has passed and darkness has descended; keeps awakening possible.

selected.text: The Call of God hath been raised, yet most of the people hear not. The Most Exalted Pen hath moved, yet most of the people understand not. The horizon of the All-Merciful hath been illumined, yet the people see not. Vain imaginings have held them back, and they perceive not
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s fourfold statement that the call is raised, the Pen moves and the horizon shines, yet people hear, understand and see not; a concise sensory sequence.

selected.text: Despite this sanctifying melody of the Abha Beauty that has reverberated throughout this infinite space, the helpless people of lethargy remain bewildered and confused like the deaf, saying "Where is that divine melody? Where is that merciful cry? Where is that heavenly song?"
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing people who, like the deaf, ask where the divine melody is while it reverberates through space; carries the image of unheard music.

selected.text: How many souls were occupied day and night with the remembrance of God, yet when He rent asunder the veils and appeared from the horizon of grace and bounty, they all became occupied with their own desires and were deprived and kept back from Him, save those whom thy Lord wished.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that souls occupied day and night with the remembrance of God turned to their own desires when He appeared; devotion without recognition.

selected.text: Nevertheless, none responded. If any soul were to observe with an eye of justice, he would instantly proclaim "I believe in God, the Lord of all worlds." However, eyes are afflicted with the soreness of vain imaginings and ears are blocked with the cotton of ignorance and unawareness.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that one who looked with an eye of justice would believe, but eyes are sore with vain imaginings and ears blocked with ignorance; ties recognition to justice.

selected.text: that He may, with the finger of His power, rend asunder the veils that have hindered men, and withhold them not from beholding the lights of the Sun of Revelation. A hundred thousand regrets that they have deprived themselves of His infinite bounties and occupied themselves with worthless trifles that neither nourish nor satisfy. Ere long they shall testify to their own loss
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking that God rend asunder the veils that hinder men from beholding the Sun of Revelation; prayer for others.

selected.text: Being overcome by the drunkenness of corrupt inclinations, the people of the earth find themselves in a state of stupor. They are, therefore, debarred from the wondrous signs of God, are prevented from attaining the ultimate goal and are deprived of the liberal effusions of divine grace.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: Their sight was blinded and their insight prevented from beholding the lights. Their ears were deaf to the breezes of the kingdom of mysteries. Their breasts were constricted by their fall into the pit of suppositions and vain imaginings and their descent into the corner of forgetfulness.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing sight blinded, ears deaf to the breezes of the Kingdom and breasts constricted in the pit of suppositions; a full sensory picture.

selected.text: The Tree crieth out, yet the people understand not. The Book speaketh with truth, yet mankind perceive not. Man uttereth speech, yet the people hear not. The Beloved giveth glad tidings to creation of this Revelation, yet they turn not unto it. The Spirit informeth them, yet they know not.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s litany of the Tree crying out, the Book speaking and the Spirit informing while people perceive not; memorable repetition of unheard speech.

selected.text: Glory be to God! What heedlessness hath seized them all - they have forsaken the ocean of divine meanings and turned to the salt and bitter pools. Though the Sun of knowledge shineth from the horizon of heaven, they have nonetheless clung to and sought after the ignorant ones of the earth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that people forsake the ocean of divine meanings for salt pools and seek out the ignorant ones of the earth; an image of misdirected seeking.

selected.text: Glory be to God! The poison of heedlessness hath affected all limbs, members and veins, and hath prevented all from attaining to understanding and awareness. Now they are seen to be in the throes of death, save those souls who have been healed with the Supreme Medicine of the Most Great Name.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the poison of heedlessness in every limb, save for those healed by the Supreme Medicine of the Most Great Name; heedlessness as illness with a remedy.

selected.text: The verses have been sent down and the signs have appeared, yet ye know not. All things have testified to the Creator of heaven, yet ye are as dead. How long will ye look to yourselves? This is the Spirit of God - behold ye bear witness! We draw you near through the cords of grace, yet ye flee.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking how long people will look to themselves while He draws them near through the cords of grace and they flee; a personal call to response.

selected.text: Most wondrous of all things is that, despite this Most Great Revelation and supreme power, none hath reflected upon the nature of the Cause. Rather, all cling to vain imaginings and remain veiled from the Beauty of certitude. Thus hath it been aforetime and thus shall it be unto the end of ends.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that despite this Revelation none has reflected on the nature of the Cause, as it was aforetime; stresses the absence of reflection.

selected.text: A hundred thousand pities that the heedless and ignorant servants are unaware and veiled from this most great bounty and supreme favor! What is the cause of awareness and what is the reason for mindfulness? The signs have encompassed the world and the evidences have filled the realm of existence.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking what is the cause of awareness and mindfulness when the signs have encompassed the world; poses the guide’s central question.

selected.text: They hear the call and behold Him Who summoneth them morn and eve, yet they draw not nigh, for they have followed every remote scholar. … He calleth them unto God while they hasten unto the idol. They are verily among the people of the coffin in the Tablet of thy Lord, the Most High, the Most Great
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing people who hear the call yet follow every remote scholar and hasten to the idol; borrowed authority.

selected.text: This is a Day wherein the Dawn proclaimeth, saying: "By God! The Morn of the Divine Manifestation hath breathed forth, yet the people are in a wondrous slumber." And the Sun crieth out, saying: "The Sun of Truth hath shone forth from the horizon of Will, yet the people are in heedlessness and error
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh giving voice to the Dawn and the Sun, which proclaim that the people are in a wondrous slumber; creation itself testifies to heedlessness.

selected.text: Despite this, the people of Iran are caught in the sleep of unconsciousness - the house unaware of its owner, the East heedless of the rising of the Sun of Truth, nay rather in constant denial. How has a Cause of such magnitude, which has amazed the world, remained unspoken among the ignorant ones?
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing the house unaware of its owner and the East heedless of the rising Sun of Truth; the homecoming image in its regional setting.

selected.text: Say: O people of the earth! By God, the heart of the world hath been set ablaze by the call of your Lord, the All-Merciful. What aileth you that ye are not set ablaze? Ye behold and recognize, yet deny and remain ignorant. Those who dwell in the realms of the seen and the unseen are bewildered at you.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking the people of the earth why they are not set ablaze when they behold and recognize yet deny; ends the opening with a direct summons.

selected.text: This servant is bewildered at how one could be deprived of the sweet-scented breezes while standing in the midst of a rose garden. The light is manifest, the fire is ablaze, and the call is raised, yet the affairs of this fleeting world have prevented the senses from beholding, perceiving, and hearing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh’s wonder that one could be deprived of sweet-scented breezes while standing in a rose garden; a memorable image of nearness unnoticed.

selected.text: Today the world--that is, humankind--is heedless. By the life of God! If they were to find even less than a needle's eye of the divine fragrance, they would cast down the idols of fancy and imagination with the hand of certitude and, detached from all else, would arise to mention, praise and serve the Cause.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh affirming that less than a needle’s eye of divine fragrance would lead people to cast down the idols of fancy and arise to serve; awakening leads to service.

selected.text: Yet have the people debarred themselves from these holy and fresh fruits. Such hath ever been the way of My creatures since before that which hath no before, and shall continue until the end which no learned one can reckon. They draw not nigh unto it save by casting stones of idle fancy and vain imaginings
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people have ever debarred themselves from holy fruits, approaching only with stones of idle fancy; states the pattern across the ages.

selected.text: All people were awaiting the days of God, yet when the Sun of Revelation shone forth from the horizon of the heaven of divine will, all were heedless of Him and occupied with and turned to other than Him, except for those souls who heard the divine call with the ear of the heart and turned toward His horizon.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing all awaiting the days of God yet turning elsewhere, save those who heard with the ear of the heart; distinguishes hearing with the heart.

selected.text: Another reason is the burning of this ephemeral one's heart, for he observes that while the Sun of loving-kindness is shining, the ocean of mercy is manifest, and the heaven of grace is raised high, most people remain heedless thereof and persist in hypocrisy, regarding mercy as vengeance and glory as abasement.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that most people regard mercy as vengeance and glory as abasement; inverted perception of grace.

selected.text: The Ocean of Life hath appeared in the contingent world, yet the people remain heedless and veiled therefrom, nay rather, they are seen to turn away. He calleth with the utmost loving-kindness and bounty, guiding and directing the thirsty ones unto Himself, yet none turneth towards Him save whom his Lord willeth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Ocean of Life calling the thirsty with loving-kindness while few turn toward it; nourishment offered.

selected.text: The world hath been set ablaze by the Word of the Ancient King, yet the people remain heedless thereof, as if they were among the dead. God had counseled His servants to regard this Revelation with His eyes - this after countless other counsels which none can reckon save God, the All-Knowing, the All-Encompassing.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recalling God’s counsel to His servants to regard this Revelation with His eyes; the guide’s clearest call to independent perception.

selected.text: I see the people of Paris like bees and ants, coming and going in swarms, moving and stirring like waves, extremely busy - but if you ask what they are doing and why they are moving about, they are completely unaware of their origin and end, and seek no perfection beyond eating, sleeping and immersion in desires.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá in Paris likening busy crowds to bees and ants unaware of their origin and end; a distinctive observation of restless activity.

selected.text: The rivers have flowed, the winds have blown, the mountains have passed away, and the branches have been scattered, yet the people remain in strange slumber. The call hath been raised between earth and heaven and the world hath been illumined by the lights of the Revelation, yet the people remain in evident delusion.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing rivers flowing, mountains passing away and the world illumined while the people remain in strange slumber; creation transformed yet unnoticed.

selected.text: The verses have been sent down, the evidences are manifest, the path is clear, and the balance is set up, yet the people are witnessed to be in great heedlessness and behind a mighty veil. The heavenly food descends in every moment from the heaven of the favor of the Lord of the Worlds, yet the people remain unaware.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that heavenly food descends at every moment while the people remain unaware; nourishment offered continually.

selected.text: When that World-Protecting Sovereign and Kind Friend removed the veil and made the lofty pavilion of heaven His royal crown's dwelling place and placed the diadem of glory upon His head, all turned away their faces, closed their eyes, fell asleep, concealed the mystery, spoke not a word, and strung not the pearls of wisdom.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing how, when the Sovereign removed the veil, all closed their eyes and strung not the pearls of wisdom; a narrative of a moment missed.

selected.text: It is very strange that notwithstanding there clear demonstrations there are ever so many men who are negligent of God; although they know that He has created all these lower creatures to serve and remind them. People are entirely engrossed with material pursuits and they have become entirely inadvertent of their own Creator.
selected.reason: Reported words of ‘Abdu’l-Bahá near Tiberias that people engrossed in material pursuits forget the Creator whose creatures serve and remind them; links nature with remembrance.

selected.text: The fragrances of that which hath streamed from the Most Exalted Pen have encompassed all things, yet the people are in strange heedlessness. The Cry hath been raised, yet they slumber; nay, they are as the dead, save him whom the breeze of reunion hath stirred and whom the hand of grace hath admitted into an exalted station.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Cry raised while the people slumber, save him whom the breeze of reunion has stirred; grace that awakens.

selected.text: Great is the Cause, and great is the Day, yet the people are heedless and barren. How many souls are occupied day and night with the mention of His appearance, beseeching and hoping to attain His presence. Yet when the Sun of Truth shone forth from the Dayspring of God's Will, some denied, others turned away, and a group hesitated
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing souls who prayed to attain His presence and then denied, turned away or hesitated; distinguishes kinds of failed response.

selected.text: the graves in the name of thy Lord, the All-Forgiving! Say: O ye who lie in the tomb! The Promised One hath come, and the Sovereign of existence hath appeared in His mighty glory. How long will ye slumber in the cradle of vain imaginings? Arise at My leave and My call
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh calling those who lie in the tomb to arise, for the Promised One has come; resurrection as renewal.

selected.text: after the lights of the Sun of inner meanings dawned and the waves of the ocean of divine utterance surged forth, all turned away. Would that they had been content with mere rejection! They attributed to Him that which the Jews did not attribute to the Spirit (Christ), nor did the idolaters and others speak about the Seal of the Prophets
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh noting that people not only rejected Him but attributed to Him what was not said of Christ or the Seal of the Prophets; rejection turned to calumny.

selected.text: Strange it is that they have not yet understood the Day of God, for had they done so, they would not have occupied themselves with the mention of aught else. He saith: 'The Kingdom on that Day shall be God's,' and likewise He saith: 'And thy Lord shall come with angels rank on rank.' Yet all remain heedless and deprived of this sealed wine.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh citing the Qur’anic verses on the Day of God and observing that all remain deprived of this sealed wine; scripture recited but not recognized.

selected.text: The Sun hath dawned from the horizon of proof, and the Nightingale of divine knowledge hath warbled upon the branches, and the Spirit hath cried out at the midmost heart of creation - yet the people remain sunk in slumber. They have not awakened at the call of God, nor have they been stirred by this Spirit whereby the world hath been shaken.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the Sun dawning, the Nightingale warbling and the Spirit crying out while the people sleep; joins light and sound in one call.

selected.text: Most astonishing of all is that none hath understood, nor doth understand, the root of the matter, yet they speak whatsoever their idle fancies prompt them to speak. Behold the baseness of their station, that some of the ignorant ones have sought to adduce proofs from "Him Whom God shall make manifest" while remaining deprived of His very Self
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh remarking that none has understood the root of the matter, yet all speak as their idle fancies prompt; examines confident speech without understanding.

selected.text: The people are heedless and debarred from the ocean of knowledge. Consider the followers of the Qur'an, how they were veiled and kept far removed by the vain sayings of the ancients. The Sun of certitude is shining and the ocean of knowledge is surging, yet they still cling to the people of conjecture and hold fast to the hem of idle fancies.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh pointing to the followers of the Qur’an, veiled by the vain sayings of the ancients while the Sun of certitude shines; a historical example of inherited opinion.

selected.text: Glory be to God! These heedless people have preferred extinction to immortality and regarded the ignorant as learned. Today the Balance is manifest and speaketh with the most exalted utterance. It is the true Discriminator and the spiritual Identifier. Yet all are heedless of it and veiled from it, save whom God willeth, the Lord of the worlds.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that people prefer extinction to immortality and regard the ignorant as learned, though the Balance is manifest; joins worldliness with false learning.

selected.text: They hear the call of God openly, yet what is in their hearts of the idols of the worshippers preventeth them from certitude … They follow their leaders and cling to the hem of their vain imaginings - nay, they are among the abased ones. They worship the calf while thinking themselves servants of God besides Him - nay, they are among the liars
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing people who follow their leaders, cling to vain imaginings and worship the calf while thinking themselves servants of God; addresses borrowed certainty.

selected.text: Thou seest, O my God, how Thy servants have been cleaving fast to Thy names, and have been calling on them in the daytime and in the night season. No sooner, however, had He been made manifest through Whose word the kingdom of names and the heaven of eternity were created, than they broke away from Him and disbelieved in the greatest of Thy signs.
selected.reason: Mandatory inclusion: exact selected wording lies in a catalogue-authorized paragraph of this translation version.

selected.text: From the beginning of the Cause this Wronged One, alone and without any veil or covering, called out with His loudest voice unto the rulers and ministers and divines and jurisprudents and philosophers, summoning all to the Most Sublime Horizon. Nevertheless, the heedless and ignorant servants have not awakened nor drunk from the ocean of knowledge.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh recounting that He called alone to rulers, ministers, divines and philosophers while the heedless did not awaken; a narrative of proclamation unheeded.

selected.text: The Beloved of the world lamenteth for Himself and saith: The peoples enter temples, churches, mosques and cloisters in My name, yet they are heedless of My Self, turn away from My presence, and do that which causeth My breast to be straitened and My heart, My Pen, the dwellers of the pavilion of My glory and the tabernacle of My grandeur to lament.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh lamenting that peoples enter temples, churches, mosques and cloisters in His name yet are heedless of His Self; the guide’s most concrete picture of worship that misses its object.

selected.text: Were the heedless world and ignorant people possessed of insight, they would have observed the penetrating power of the Word and the might of God's Will, would have conducted themselves with due measure, and would have cast aside the veils of idle fancies and vain imaginings which have held back most of humanity from the Lord of the Day of Resurrection.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh stating that with insight people would observe the power of the Word and conduct themselves with due measure; links insight to conduct.

selected.text: Has not the time come for those who sleep to awaken and those who are heedless to become aware? Do they think they shall not depart, shall not enter the graves, shall not be gathered tomorrow and questioned? Far from it! Their imaginings are false, their abode is the abyss, and they shall find none to protect them unless they return to God, the Lord of creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking whether the sleeping think they shall not depart, enter the grave and be questioned; joins heedlessness to mortality.

selected.text: You observe that all the people of the world are caught in the sleep of heedlessness. They have completely forgotten God. All are engaged in war and strife and are in loss and affliction. Like tiny worms in the depths of the earth they strive to make a nest and dwelling, while one flood will destroy their nest and dwelling. Despite this they do not become aware.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá likening people absorbed in strife to tiny worms building nests that one flood will destroy; a vivid image of misplaced effort.

selected.text: O my brother! Although the horizon of the Manifestation is resplendent and illumined with the Sun of Divine Beauty, yet most men are seen to be bewildered and perplexed, nay, dead and lost. Most strange it is that they have not yet found the sweetness of the most pure wine, and have not attained to that exalted station of nearness which is the recognition of God.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh, addressing “my brother”, observing that most men, though the horizon is illumined, have not found the sweetness of the most pure wine or the nearness of recognition; names recognition as nearness.

selected.text: Nevertheless, when the gate of reunion was opened and the breeze of attainment wafted, all remained heedless and unconscious in the wilderness of negligence, save whom God willed. Those who counted themselves among the foremost and considered themselves preeminent in knowledge and insight were deprived of His presence and veiled from the purpose and cause of creation.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that those who considered themselves preeminent in knowledge and insight were veiled when the gate of reunion opened; knowledge offers no automatic protection.

selected.text: Yet despite these mighty outpourings, souls remain veiled and hearts turn away. Some soar on the wings of vain imaginings, while others make their dwelling in the lowest depths - these are as the cattle. Some are deprived of a drop from the Most Great Ocean, and some remain bereft of a particle from the Most Luminous Sun. How wretched is the abode of the wavering ones!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing some who soar on vain imaginings and others who dwell in the lowest depths, deprived of a drop of the Ocean; the varied forms of veiling.

selected.text: Glory be to God! This servant is astonished at the condition of people. A group of Christians from various regions have shown sincerity and affection, and have come to this land solely to investigate and examine. Although they did not attain the [Holy] Presence, they were blessed for several days to attain the presence of the Most Great
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing Christians from various regions who came to this land solely to investigate and examine; a narrative example of sincere inquiry.

selected.text: Heedlessness hath so seized the world that every living soul is bewildered. How many souls have been observed whose song was raised at one hour, while at another their lamentation and wailing was heard. Are they assured by the fidelity of the world? How can this be when it declareth at all times and confesseth its transience, and showeth forth its changes and variations?
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people trust the fidelity of a world that constantly confesses its own transience; a clear statement of the passing world.

selected.text: The earth is changed to another earth and the heaven to another heaven, yet the people of the world remain heedless and veiled. The dwellers of the graves have arisen at the breath of revelation of the Self-Subsisting Lord, while the living souls are seen as if dead. The intoxication of pride and heedlessness has encompassed the world and deprived it of the Ancient Lord.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing the dwellers of the graves arising at the breath of revelation while the living seem dead; distinguishes spiritual from physical life.

selected.text: Indeed, there is nothing worse in the world than unconsciousness. These Iranians are both unconscious and self-conceited. They imagine each one of them is the Plato of the age while they know nothing. You met the cream of Iranian ministers in Paris, and likewise went to Iran and observed its notables. The greatest prince of Iran was Zillu's-Sultan - you saw what he was like.
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing self-conceited people who each imagine themselves the Plato of the age while knowing nothing; the guide’s link to presumed wisdom.

selected.text: Today the proof itself calleth aloud, and all evidence summoneth mankind to a Cause the like of which, from the beginning of creation until now, hath never appeared. Such is the heedlessness of the people that they have turned away from Him Who hath brought verses that equal all divine books past and future, and have occupied themselves with souls who are not worthy of mention.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing proofs calling aloud to an unparalleled Cause while people occupy themselves with souls not worthy of mention; misplaced attention.

selected.text: O beloved of my heart! This servant is at every moment immersed in the ocean of wonderment, for he observes that the lights of the Manifestation have encompassed the world and the effulgences of the Sun of Truth have taken hold of the entire earth; nevertheless, all are either asleep on the couch of heedlessness or wandering in the desert of ignorance, save whom my Lord willeth.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh describing this servant’s wonder that all are asleep or wandering though the lights of the Manifestation encompass the world; a meditation on gift withheld.

selected.text: Strange it is that, although God, exalted and glorified be He, hath bestowed sight and consciousness and taste, sweet and fresh water appeareth to them the same as salt and bitter - nay, the latter is deemed more excellent and preferable. As can be plainly observed, they have forsaken the Most Great Ocean and turned instead to putrid waters that have stagnated for years in the pool of self.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh marvelling that people endowed with sight and taste prefer stagnant, bitter water to the Most Great Ocean; a memorable image of perverted judgment.

selected.text: Nevertheless, they were seen to be as stones, having no movement, or as those struck down, as God the Exalted hath said: "And thou mightest have seen the people therein struck down as though they were the hollow trunks of palm-trees." … Beseech ye God to awaken the heedless ones, to guide the seekers unto their goal, and to not deprive His servants of this fragrance that hath perfumed the world
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh likening people to hollow palm-trunks and bidding the friends beseech God to awaken the heedless and guide the seekers; joins warning with prayer for others.

selected.text: But these people are so deeply asleep that even the trumpet of Israfil would not awaken them, let alone the sound and blast of cholera and the trumpet of the plague of persecution. Glory be to God! These ignorant people understood expulsion from Paradise as one of Satan's miracles, and consider the spread of cholera as disrespect to Khwajih Bu-'Ali. What ignorance is this and what foolishness
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observing that people sleep so deeply that neither cholera nor persecution awakens them; a particular calamity kept in its setting.

selected.text: Yet another group remained in the sleep of heedlessness, lying upon the bed of error, remaining unconscious in their stupor and intoxicated in their drunkenness, gathering blindly together, appearing deaf, dumb, ignorant, unlearned and indolent, deprived of the bounties of this Most Great Sea and the effulgences of this Most Glorious Luminary. How wretched is the state of those who are deprived!
selected.reason: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describing a group lying in the sleep of heedlessness, deaf, dumb and deprived of the Most Great Sea; contrasts with the awakened.

selected.text: The sweet waters of life are present and visible, yet the people, heedless, turn to and occupy themselves with putrid waters. Vain imaginings have so deceived them that they have doubted the appearance of God and His presence, after He hath appeared in truth from this luminous station. Behold their paucity of understanding: they invoke the Names morning and evening, yet deny Him Who created them.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh observing that people invoke the Names morning and evening yet deny Him Who created them; names without the reality they signify.

selected.text: Glory be to God! Despite this supreme grace which hath encompassed both the seen and unseen worlds, the people remain heedless and veiled. What intoxication hath seized the world of knowledge? Despite the raising of the call and the appearance of the banners of the Lord of all beings, all remain asleep in the slumber of heedlessness. The cry hath not awakened them and the trumpet hath had no effect.
selected.reason: Bahá’u’lláh asking what intoxication has seized the world of knowledge when neither cry nor trumpet awakens it; a challenge to the learned.

selected.text: The mass of the people are occupied with self and worldly desire, are immersed in the ocean of the nether world and are captives of the world of nature, save those souls who have been freed from the chains and fetters of the material world and, like unto swift-flying birds, are soaring in this unbounded realm.

selected.text: O army of God! Today, in this world, every people is wandering astray in its own desert, moving here and there according to the dictates of its fancies and whims, pursuing its own particular caprice. Amongst all the teeming masses of the earth, only this community of the Most Great Name is free and clear of human schemes and hath no selfish purpose to promote. Alone amongst them all, this people hath arisen with aims purified of self, following the Teachings of God, most eagerly toiling and striving toward a single goal: to turn this nether dust into high heaven, to make of this world a mirror for the Kingdom, to change this world into a different world, and cause all humankind to adopt the ways of righteousness and a new manner of life.

Alone amongst them all, this people hath arisen with aims purified of self, following the Teachings of God, most eagerly toiling and striving toward a single goal: to turn this nether dust into high heaven, to make of this world a mirror for the Kingdom, to change this world into a different world, and cause all humankind to adopt the ways of righteousness and a new manner of life.
